name: button
description: The primary action: an ink pill that presses under your finger, refuses a double tap, never flashes a spinner, and can turn into a check when the thing is done. Secondary, text, and destructive variants ship in the same file.
avoidWhen: Do not use for navigation rows or inline text links. Do not use AppDestructiveButton without a cancel beside it.

ux.behaviour: The pill scales to 0.97 while pressed and springs back on release, with a click haptic when the tap lands; ripple and scale share one interactionSource
ux.why: You feel the button take the tap; the pill is the brand
ux.reducedMotion: No scale; ripple and haptic only

ux.behaviour: A second tap within 400 ms of the first is ignored, and taps are ignored while loading or success
ux.why: Nobody pays twice because the network was slow

ux.behaviour: The spinner appears only after 150 ms and stays at least 500 ms; the label stays in the tree at alpha 0 so the width holds
ux.why: A fast call is just fast; a slow one shows one steady spinner, not a blink
ux.reducedMotion: Label alpha jumps instead of fading; timing unchanged

ux.behaviour: Loading keeps primary colours and TalkBack reads Loading; it is not disabled
ux.why: Gray means you cannot; a spinner means wait

ux.behaviour: success swaps the label for a check with a confirm haptic and reads Done; the caller holds it about 800 ms and then navigates
ux.why: The thing you did gets acknowledged where you did it

ux.behaviour: Secondary is a quiet gray fill, text is bare, destructive is red text and never a red fill
ux.why: One dark pill per section says what matters; red text says careful without shouting

aiHints: Keep enabled as the caller's enabled; ignore clicks while loading instead of setting enabled = !loading
Set loading the moment the request starts; the button decides whether a spinner is worth showing
For success, set success = true when the response lands, delay about 800 ms, then navigate; do not leave it true
Do not replace the label with the spinner; overlay it so the width does not jump
One AppButton per screen section; the rest are AppSecondaryButton or AppTextButton
AppDestructiveButton goes beside a cancel; the destructive-confirmation pattern owns the dialog
Pass localized loadingStateDescription and successStateDescription from your strings
